issue.title: Add an endpoint mode to the pi harness

error_messages: the pi harness has no explicit-endpoint mode: pi resolves models through its own catalogue. Add the endpoint to pi's models.json once, then select it with --model <provider>/<model>.

analysis.summary: This is a deliberate refusal, not a missing capability. PiHarness.__init__ (benchkit/harness/pi.py:58-62) raises SystemExit the moment base_url is set, and the module docstring (38-41) argues the case: writing a provider into the user's ~/.pi/agent/models.json would change how their editor behaves. The premise is right; the conclusion does not follow, and the repo already disproves it twice. Both sibling adapters solve the same problem the same way: opencode writes a throwaway config beside the temp workspace and points the tool at it with OPENCODE_CONFIG (opencode.py:154-190), and claude-code writes a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR only when uses_endpoint is set (claudecode.py:204-216, 241-253). pi has the identical seam already wired: _catalogue_path() (pi.py:114-116) resolves PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR before ~/.pi/agent, and _env() (81-86) already injects PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR into the subprocess environment when self.agent_dir is set. The feature is therefore an extension along an existing axis, not a new architecture.
analysis.details: Data flow today: cmd_harness reads endpoint from --endpoint or BENCH_HARNESS_ENDPOINT (cli.py:185), passes it through _endpoint_kw (255-259) which returns {'base_url': endpoint} for any harness regardless of the name it is given, then constructs H.get(args.harness, base_url=...) - and PiHarness dies in its constructor before model resolution. Target flow: PiHarness stores base_url, exposes uses_endpoint, and in prepare() copies the user's catalogue (read-only) into the run's temp dir, adds one synthetic OpenAI-compatible provider pointing at the endpoint, writes that copy, and sets PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to the temp dir for the subprocess only. Nothing under the user's home is opened for writing. Two constraints fall out. First, the injected provider must satisfy _provider_addressable() (pi.py:190-195) so _argv() (176-188) passes --provider/--model correctly. Second, the endpoint path must skip _catalogue()-based validation, since the served model is not in the user's catalogue - opencode's available() endpoint branch (122-133), which probes the OpenAI-compatible /models URL directly, is the precedent. Note on the repo hard rules: tests/test_harness_models.py:123-126 must be rewritten, but that is a harness unit test, not a benchmark task's tests/asserts/check - the 'never edit a task's tests to make a model pass' rule does not apply.

decision_record.root_cause: Not a missing capability but a deliberate refusal: PiHarness.__init__ (benchkit/harness/pi.py:58-62) raises SystemExit whenever base_url is set, on the correct premise that a benchmark must not rewrite ~/.pi/agent/models.json. The conclusion does not follow - opencode (OPENCODE_CONFIG) and claude-code (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) both already point their tool at a throwaway config, and pi has the identical seam wired via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR in _env (81-86) and _catalogue_path (114-116).

selected_option.name: Endpoint mode plus consistent three-harness contract and docs
selected_option.summary: Copy the user's pi catalogue into the run's temp dir, inject one synthetic endpoint provider, expose it via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR for the subprocess only, and correct every doc and test that asserts pi cannot take an endpoint.

decision_record.residual_risk: In endpoint mode the model cannot be validated against the user's catalogue, so a wrong --model surfaces at run time rather than at selection time; mitigate by probing the endpoint's /v1/models in available(), as opencode already does. Rewriting tests/test_harness_models.py:123-126 is required and permitted - it is a harness unit test, not a benchmark task's tests/asserts/check.
